dedupe_keys.name: fao giews agricultural stress index system asis global drought indicators for cropland and pasture 1 km 1984 to present

description: Satellite-based indicators that flag cropland and pasture areas likely to be under water stress (drought), updated every dekad (10 days). The ASIS pages say seasonal indicators, the Agricultural Stress Index, Drought Intensity and the Weighted Mean Vegetation Health Index, combine vegetation and land surface temperature data with cropping cycles from historical data and a global crop mask, for two seasons and as dekadal, annual and multi-annual products; non-seasonal indicators such as NDVI anomaly and the progress of season (start, maximum and end from long-term NDVI) are also given, with results aggregated to GAUL level 2 regions and country pages. The data access page says all ASIS rasters (global, 1 km, 1984 to present, more than 16,000 layers) can be viewed in the FAO Agro-informatics Platform and ArcGIS Online, are served as WMTS image services, and are on Google Earth Engine on request, under CC BY 4.0 with FAO database terms of use. Coverage is global cropland and pasture. Caveats: phenology is a static long-term average and errors in the crop mask can distort seasonal indicators. For simulation it gives a long, consistent drought history for farm areas, to drive crop loss, food supply and water demand scenarios. Related catalogue records include the GEOGLAM Crop Monitor and FAO DIEM EVE flood monitoring.
